environment: short, before a high vowel or glide
notes: Raised short allophone; [e] is always followed by a high vowel or glide and never occurs word-finally or long except by compensatory lengthening. Garvin's surface contrast of e and ɛ is analysed as subphonemic (p. 284).
The phonetic norm of the single mid front vowel phoneme (p. 284).

environment: Kiti dialect, before j and w
notes: Garvin (n.d.: 8-9) quoted by Rehg: in Kiti the only mid front vowel phoneme has a closed allophone [e] before y and w, an open allophone [ɛ] elsewhere; long e is always [ɛː].
